newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bank Austria dividend up, positive on 97. [corrected 09:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria dividend up, positive on 97. [corrected 09:45 GMT]

text.p: Bank Austria, the country's top bank, said on Thursday it would raise its 1996 dividend to 12 schillings per share from 10 schillings last year and forecast the current year would bring improved earnings.
In a statement, the bank said it expected a "satisfactory earnings development" for its core parent bank.

The bank, which recently took control of its main competitor Creditanstalt, traced the improvement to an "easing of the credit risk situation and internal cost cutting measures" (corrects from ...easing of credit, the risk situation... to clarify that credit risk situation and not credit is eased).

For the combined Bank Austria/Creditanstalt group, operating profit in the first four months of the year rose some 18 percent to 3.907 billion schilligs, finance chief Franz Zwickel told a news conference.
Bank Austria last week reported a 29 percent increase in first-quarter parent operating profit to 1.395 billion schillings.
However, it warned last week's figures could not simply be multiplied by four to reach either full year group or parent earnings.

Group net profit in 1996 dropped an unexpectedly large 39 percent to 1.587 billion schillings. First quarter operating profit, consolidated to include most Creditanstalt units, was at 3.565 billion schillings, the bank said last week.
Bank Austria acquired the state's 70 percent voting stake in Creditanstalt in January for 17 billion schillings in cash.
The merger, Austria's biggest since World War Two, created a banking giant with assets valued at some 1.55 billion schillings at the end of March. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 274
